questions.text:
If the list of letters [latex]P, R, S, T, U[/latex] is an arithmetic sequence, which of the following are also in arithmetic sequence?
I. [latex]2P,2R,2S,2T,2U[/latex]
II. [latex]P-3,R-3,S-3,T-3,U-3[/latex]
III. [latex]P^2, R^2, S^2, T^2, U^2[/latex]
questions.solution:
If the common difference is d:
- I: doubling gives common difference 2d [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] AP
- II: subtracting 3 keeps difference d [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] AP
- III: squares, e.g. 1, 2, 3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1, 4, 9 (differences 3, 5) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not AP

Answer: I and II

questions.text: Four branches of a company are located at M, N, O and P. M is north of N at a distance of 4km; P is south of O at a distance of 2 km; N is southeast of O by 1km. What is the distance between M and P in km?
questions.solution:
Take O = (0, 0). Then P = (0, [latex]-[/latex]2) and N = (0.707, [latex]-[/latex]0.707) (1 km south-east). M is 4 km north of N: M = (0.707, 3.293).

MP = [latex]\sqrt{0.707^2+5.293^2}=\sqrt{0.5+28.02}\approx5.34[/latex] km

Answer: 5.34

questions.text: In a triangle [latex]PQR,PS[/latex] is the angle bisector of [latex]\angle QPR \text{ and } \angle QPS =60^\circ[/latex]. What is the length of [latex]PS[/latex] ?
questions.solution:
[latex]\angle QPR=120^\circ[/latex]. Area of PQR = area of PQS + area of PSR:

[latex]\frac12 rq\sin120^\circ=\frac12 r\cdot PS\sin60^\circ+\frac12 q\cdot PS\sin60^\circ[/latex]

Since [latex]\sin120^\circ=\sin60^\circ[/latex]: [latex]rq=PS(r+q)\Rightarrow PS=\frac{qr}{q+r}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\frac{qr}{q+r}[/latex]

questions.text:
If p, q, r, s are distinct integers such that:[latex]f(p,q,r,s)= max (p,q,r,s)[/latex]
[latex]g(p,q,r,s)= min (p,q,r,s) [/latex]
[latex]h (p, q, r, s) = \text {remainder of } \frac{(p \times q)} {(r \times s)} \text{ if } (p \times q) \gt (r \times s)[/latex]
[latex]\text{ or remainder of } \frac {(r \times s)}{(p \times q)} \text{ if } (r \times s) \gt (p \times q)[/latex]

Also a function [latex]fgh(p,q,r,s)=f(p,q,r,s) \times g(p,q,r,s) \times h(p,q,r,s)[/latex]
Also the same operations are valid with two variable functions of the form [latex]f(p,q)[/latex]
What is the value of [latex]fg(h(2,5,7,3),4,6,8)[/latex]?
questions.solution:
h(2, 5, 7, 3): p [latex]\times[/latex] q = 10, r [latex]\times[/latex] s = 21. 21 [latex]\gt[/latex] 10, so h = 21 mod 10 = 1.

fg(1, 4, 6, 8) = max [latex]\times[/latex] min = 8 [latex]\times[/latex] 1 = 8

Answer: 8

questions.text: Out of the following 4 sentences, select the most suitable sentence with respect to grammar and usage:
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Option 2: "information" is uncountable, so "were no" is wrong.
- Option 3: "real useful" should be "really useful".
- Option 4: "would not had been" should be "would not have been".

Option 1 is correct.

Answer: Since the report lacked needed information, it was of no use to them
